r0.why: Differential survival and reproduction from relative fitness of observable traits, key mechanism changing heritable traits in 1,2.

r1.why: Genotypic/phenotypic variation, favoured traits passed on and more common in fixed environment, Darwin's definition in 4-7,43.

r2.why: Best adapted more likely to survive, inevitable selection given heritable variation, primary explanation despite drift in 22,44,45.

r3.why: Many factors, environmental adaptation, sexual selection, Darwin's contrast with intentional artificial selection by breeders in 3,11-13,17.

r4.why: Leonardo at turn of 16th century on forms selected by fit to environment, uniformitarianism making species-scale change plausible in 32,33,36,37.

r5.why: Joint 1858 papers, 1859 Origin explaining adaptation and speciation, no valid heredity theory, mid-20th-century modern synthesis in 16,18,19,42.

r6.why: Niche change gives microevolution, broader change macroevolution, new species when traits radically differ in 8-10.
